Advanced ATC

Satellite-Based Augmentation System

A satellite navigation system that augments GNSS signals, providing improved accuracy, integrity, and availability for aviation, including SBAS services like WAAS, EGNOS, GAGAN, and MSAS (ICAO Annex 10, Doc 9849).

Quick answer: A satellite navigation system that augments GNSS signals, providing improved accuracy, integrity, and availability for aviation, including SBAS services like WAAS, EGNOS, GAGAN, and MSAS (ICAO Annex 10, Doc 9849).

Why it matters

Questions and answers

Questions and answers

What is Satellite-Based Augmentation System?

In this glossary, Satellite-Based Augmentation System refers to: A satellite navigation system that augments GNSS signals, providing improved accuracy, integrity, and availability for aviation, including SBAS services like WAAS, EGNOS, GAGAN, and MSAS (ICAO Annex 10, Doc 9849).

How is Satellite-Based Augmentation System used in aviation?

In aviation communication, this term appears in contexts such as: "The Satellite-Based Augmentation System provides precision approach capability for equipped aircraft at designated airports."

Why does Satellite-Based Augmentation System matter in aviation?

Satellite-Based Augmentation System matters because it supports clear communication in Advanced ATC contexts for Pilots, Air Traffic Controllers, and Cabin Crew. It also connects to aviation training and exam language such as ICAO Level 4, ICAO Level 5, ICAO Level 6, and EASA FCL.055.

Who uses Satellite-Based Augmentation System?

Satellite-Based Augmentation System is mainly used by Pilots, Air Traffic Controllers, and Cabin Crew.

What category does Satellite-Based Augmentation System belong to?

In this glossary, Satellite-Based Augmentation System is grouped under Advanced ATC. Related pages in this category explain adjacent procedures, commands and operational concepts.

Where does this definition come from?
